notes.title: Dualis. Episode 2 — Release
notes.content:
Hey everyone!
I'm happy to announce that [b]Episode Two of Dualis[/b] is officially out and now available on Steam.
If you’ve been waiting for the story to continue — it’s here.

A quick reminder for those who might be new to the project:
[b]Dualis[/b] is a story-driven horror thriller that combines [i]stealth-action[/i] and [i]survival horror[/i] elements, presented from an isometric perspective.
The game is released in episodes and is currently in Early Access. A total of three episodes are planned. The first is already available — and now it’s joined by the second.

[b]What to expect in Episode Two:[/b]
• [b]Two new locations[/b] — larger in scale and more visually diverse
• [b]Story progression[/b] — a faster pace and more dynamic narrative development
• [b]New enemy types[/b] and logic-based challenges
• [b]The first boss fight[/b] in the game
• On average, [b]40–60 minutes of gameplay[/b] per chapter (depending on playstyle)

[b]What’s been improved:[/b]
In addition to the new content, several improvements have been made to Episode One:
• Performance optimizations (FPS in previously heavy scenes increased to 80–120)
• Rebalanced difficulty, especially in the final section
• Bug fixes and an updated save system

[b]Dualis[/b] is an independent project that I’m doing my best to bring to completion.
Thank you to everyone who’s stayed with it — your interest is the main reason this game keeps moving forward. If you've already played Episode One — I hope the second chapter lives up to your expectations. If not — now’s a great time to dive in. Add Dualis to your wishlist, share your thoughts, and as always, [b]thank you for your support.[/b]

notes.title: Dualis. Episode Two.
notes.content:
The release of [b]Dualis Episode Two[/b] is just around the corner! I'm continuing to work on the project, and in this post, I’d like to share its current state with you.

A little about the game for those who are not yet familiar with it: 
Dualis is a story-driven horror thriller that blends stealth action and survival horror mechanics, presented from an isometric perspective. It is being released episodically and is currently available in early access on Steam, with only the first episode out so far.

It’s been a while since the release of the first episode.
Although the game wasn't a financial success, it received a warm and encouraging response from players. That feedback became my main motivation to continue development — despite the challenges and despite the financial aspect. Simply because this project is something that matters — both to me and, hopefully, to those who have already played it. With that in mind, I began working on Episode Two.

The development of Episode Two took longer than I initially expected, but it’s now nearing completion.
Over this period, significant work has been done — not just on the new episode, but also on improving the first one. Here are the key areas that have been addressed:
[list]
[*] Optimization improved: In some scenes, the framerate used to drop to 50–60 FPS. Now those same areas maintain a stable 80–120 FPS.
[*] Difficulty balance adjusted: Many players noted that the finale of Episode One felt overly punishing. While Dualis isn’t meant to be easy, the difficulty should remain fair — and that balance has now been fine-tuned.
[*] Minor bugs fixed: Including issues like broken door positions after reloads and similar small glitches.
[*] Save system improved: Previously, certain items could occasionally disappear from the inventory — this has been corrected.
[/list]
There’s still some polishing left to do, but development is actively ongoing. Big thanks to everyone who shared feedback, and a special thanks to $UpSkill$ for the detailed bug reports!

[b]Now, a bit more about Episode Two:[/b]
Just like in the first episode, players will explore [b]two main locations.[/b] However, they are now slightly larger and much more visually diverse. The [b]story[/b] also develops at a much faster pace — if the first episode unfolded very slowly, in the second one events will escalate much more rapidly.
The [b]gameplay[/b] will be expanded with new enemies, new puzzles, and the first boss fight in the game. [b]Playtime[/b] for the first episode averaged about 40–60 minutes for a new player. I expect the second episode to take about the same amount of time, meaning the total playtime for the two chapters will be around 2 hours for new players. The [b]release date[/b] for Episode Two is tentatively set for May 25, 2025. However, this may vary depending on circumstances. I will announce the final release date later, but I can assure you: any delay will not exceed two months.

Dualis exists because of your interest, support, and feedback. If you haven't added it to your wishlist yet, now’s the perfect time! You can also follow the updates to stay tuned for the release of Episode Two. Thank you to everyone who continues to support the project and its journey forward.

notes.title: Dualis.DevLog#1
notes.content:
Dualis has finally become available in steam early access, this is certainly a good thing. However, it's premature to celebrate, as this is just the beginning of a long journey.  I have already received some feedback from those who have already played the game, and in general it has been received quite warmly, but there have also been some issues that need to be addressed urgently. I decided that before starting the realization of the second episode, it is necessary to close the existing problems such as bugs. I will list the most important of them.

[b]Bugs:[/b]
[list]
[*]AI - Most of all, my attention was drawn to the behavior of zombies, sometimes they just stopped paying attention to the player, sometimes they didn't see the player point-blank, in general they could be extremely uninterested in the presence of the player. In addition, other, less significant, but still annoying bugs were found. In this regard, it was decided to completely rework the AI of enemies, it is a big job, but now, with the experience gained, I think I can make it better. 

[*]Shooting - Many people wrote that they tried not to use the gun, because shooting turned out to be quite uncomfortable. The plan is to change the mechanics of shooting and make an auto-aim on the nearest characters.

[*]Balance - The last location proved to be quite difficult to get through. I strive to keep the game interesting, not stuffy. As such, the balance of this section of the game needs to be optimized to make it more accessible to players.

[*]Animations - The character animations look pretty bad, in principle I realized this even before the release of the episode, but decided to postpone solving this problem in order not to delay the release of the game
[/list]

These are the main problems, but, of course, not all the fixes to be made, there are more minor ones, for example, sometimes enemies can clamp the character or chase if they are dead or the same item constantly falls out of enemies. These tasks I plan to close within a month or two and after that, to begin the realization of the second level.

[b]Episode 2 plans:[/b]
[list]
[*]When's the second episode?
I plan to release the second episode around December this year. I hope to be able to quickly solve the current problems in the game and start the realization of the second one. Now that the foundation of the game has been laid, the process of releasing new episodes should accelerate, all that remains is to finalize the current version and start developing new episodes.
[*]What will be in the new episodes?
In episode 2, new enemies will be introduced and Adam's ability to fight them will be used more actively. There will be new, more powerful weapons. We will also learn more about what happened in the complex and what led to the disaster. The relationship between Adam and Lily will also continue, we will learn more about the history of these characters and what challenges they will face on the way to salvation.
[/list]

That's my plans. I will try to write posts like this more often, I just enjoyed it and to keep you updated on what's going on with the game. Thanks again for your support and feedback. It's invaluable to me, only with your help will I be able to make this game better.

If you'd like to join me in developing this game, regardless of experience, you can write to the following links:

constntart@gmail.com

https://twitter.com/art_const

https://vk.com/id618282607
